text: The authors study how a trusted but computationally bounded verifier can learn to interact with one or more powerful but untrusted provers, all represented as neural networks, to solve a task, and call solutions neural interactive proofs. They introduce a unifying framework based on prover-verifier games that generalises earlier protocols, describe several new protocols with a theoretical comparison, and run experiments on a toy graph isomorphism problem and a code validation task with large language models.
title: Neural interactive proofs: learned prover-verifier protocols for trusted weak verifiers
